definition: In statistics, generalized iterative scaling (GIS) and improved iterative scaling (IIS) are two early algorithms used to fit log-linear models, notably multinomial logistic regression (MaxEnt) classifiers and extensions of it such as MaxEnt Markov models and conditional random fields.
details: These algorithms have been largely surpassed by gradient-based methods such as L-BFGS and coordinate descent algorithms.
story: Think of a lightbulb moment: the idea was always there, but someone had to point a finger at it. Here is the short version: In statistics, generalized iterative scaling (GIS) and improved iterative scaling (IIS) are two early algorithms used to fit log-linear models, notably multinomial logistic regression (MaxEnt) classifiers and extensions of it such as MaxEnt Markov models and conditional random fields. The part that makes it sing: These algorithms have been largely surpassed by gradient-based methods such as L-BFGS and coordinate descent algorithms. Once you see it, you cannot unsee it.
